title: Houthi Missile Strike — MV Rubymar
description: British-owned, Belize-flagged bulk carrier struck by two anti-ship missiles in the southern Red Sea. Vessel sustained catastrophic flooding and was abandoned by crew. Approximately 41,000 tonnes of ammonium phosphate fertilizer lost at sea, creating an environmental hazard along the shipping lane.

title: MV True Confidence Strike — Crew Casualties
description: Barbados-flagged bulk carrier struck by a Houthi anti-ship missile in the Gulf of Aden. Three crew members killed — the first confirmed fatalities directly attributable to Houthi anti-ship operations in this campaign. Surviving crew evacuated by US Navy assets.

title: MV Galaxy Leader Seizure
description: Bahamas-flagged vehicle carrier seized by Houthi naval commandos who fast-roped from a helicopter onto the vessel in the Red Sea. The 25-member crew, comprising nationals from multiple countries, remained held in Hudaydah port through mid-2025. Vessel linked to partial Israeli ownership.

title: MV Strinda Anti-Ship Missile Strike
description: Norwegian-flagged chemical tanker struck by a Houthi missile, sustaining a fire in the cargo hold. Crew reported uninjured but vessel diverted to Djibouti for emergency repairs. Strike occurred near the primary northbound shipping lane through the southern Red Sea.

title: HMS Diamond Drone Engagement
description: Royal Navy Type 45 destroyer HMS Diamond engaged and destroyed a Houthi armed drone over the Red Sea using Sea Viper missiles, marking one of the first confirmed British naval intercepts in the campaign. UK forces operating as part of Operation Prosperity Guardian multinational maritime security task force.

title: MV Cyclades Missile Strike
description: Greek-owned bulk carrier sustained missile strike damage in the central Red Sea. Crew evacuated following fire onboard. Attack reinforced the pattern of Houthi targeting of vessels with real or claimed Israeli ownership linkages, and contributed to further rerouting of traffic via the Cape of Good Hope.

title: MV Tutor Drone Attack — Engineer Killed
description: Greek-owned bulk carrier MV Tutor attacked by an explosive-laden Houthi drone boat in the Red Sea. A Filipino crew member killed and another injured. Vessel sustained severe damage and was later abandoned. One of the most destructive individual Houthi maritime attacks of the 2024 campaign.

title: Houthi Ballistic Missile — Red Sea Tanker
description: Anti-ship ballistic missile (ASBM) fired at a laden crude oil tanker transiting the northern Red Sea. Vessel sustained damage to superstructure; no casualties reported. Use of ballistic missiles against commercial shipping marked a tactical escalation in Houthi maritime interdiction capability.

title: Bab-el-Mandeb Coordinated Drone Swarm
description: Coordinated swarm of six Houthi kamikaze drones launched toward coalition naval escorts and commercial vessels near the Bab-el-Mandeb strait. All drones neutralized by USS Carney and coalition assets before reaching targets. Attack demonstrated improving Houthi swarm saturation tactics.

title: Djibouti Anchorage Drone Threat — Commercial Diversion
description: Multiple commercial vessels anchored near Djibouti reported drone activity and received UKMTO advisories to reduce exposure. Several vessels elected to hold position rather than transit the Bab-el-Mandeb, contributing to queue buildup and transit delay of 48–72 hours for southbound traffic.

title: IRGC Seizure — MSC Aries Container Ship
description: Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) naval commandos seized the Portugal-flagged container ship MSC Aries in the Strait of Hormuz, deploying from a helicopter. Vessel linked to Israeli-affiliated Zodiac Maritime. 25 crew held for weeks before release. Seizure timed one day after Iranian drone/missile strikes on Israel.

title: IRGC Seizure — MV Advantage Sweet
description: Marshall Islands-flagged crude oil tanker seized by IRGC fast boats in the Strait of Hormuz. Vessel and its 34-member crew escorted to Bandar Abbas. Action followed US seizure of Iranian crude in international waters and was assessed as a retaliatory move. Crew released after several weeks.

title: IRGC Fast Boat Harassment — Laden Tanker
description: Multiple IRGC Navy fast attack craft surrounded and harassed a laden crude oil tanker in the central Persian Gulf, demanding communications and threatening to board. Vessel was escorted by a US destroyer which intervened. Incident lasted approximately two hours before Iranian vessels withdrew.
affectedRoutes: Persian Gulf northbound crude export route

title: Mine Suspected — Fujairah Anchorage
description: Tanker at anchorage off Fujairah reported hull damage consistent with a limpet mine or underwater explosive device. UAE authorities and US Navy EOD teams investigated. No attribution confirmed publicly, but event raised threat level for tankers anchored near the primary bunkering hub at the Gulf of Oman entrance.

title: US Destroyer Intercepts IRGC Weapons Transfer
description: USS Mason intercepted a stateless dhow in the Gulf of Oman carrying anti-tank missiles, drone components, and munitions assessed to be of Iranian origin destined for Houthi forces. Crew detained for questioning and cargo confiscated. Fourth such interdiction in a 90-day period.

title: Houthi ASBM Near Strait of Hormuz
description: Houthi forces launched an anti-ship ballistic missile targeting a tanker approaching the Strait of Hormuz from the Gulf of Oman. Missile intercepted by USS Cole using SM-3 in a successful intercept that was one of only a handful of SM-3 intercepts of a ballistic missile in combat conditions globally.

title: Suez Canal Traffic Collapse — Red Sea Diversion
description: Following Houthi attacks in the Red Sea, Suez Canal northbound traffic dropped approximately 42% in January 2024 relative to the prior year. Most major container lines rerouted via the Cape of Good Hope, adding 10–14 days per voyage. Canal Authority revenue fell sharply, pressuring Egyptian foreign exchange reserves.

title: Israeli Navy Intercepts Arms Vessel — Eastern Med
description: Israeli Navy intercepted and boarded a vessel in the eastern Mediterranean assessed to be carrying advanced weapons components believed to be destined for Hezbollah via Lebanon. Cargo included guidance systems and rocket motors. Vessel crew detained; contraband transferred to Israeli custody.

title: Suspected Houthi Drone Reaches Mediterranean
description: A long-range Houthi drone assessed to have originated near the Yemeni coast was intercepted near the Nile Delta coast after transiting the Red Sea, Suez Canal corridor, and northern Sinai. If confirmed, the flight profile represented a significant extension of Houthi strike range into the Mediterranean Sea.

title: Turkish Research Vessel Detained — Cyprus EEZ Dispute
description: Turkish-flagged research vessel detained by Cypriot coast guard for operating within Cyprus's Exclusive Economic Zone without authorization. Turkey does not recognize Cyprus's EEZ claim in the disputed eastern Mediterranean maritime boundary. Diplomatic protest filed; vessel released after 18 hours.

title: PLA Navy Exercise — Strait Blockade Drill
description: People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command launched Exercise Joint Sword-2024A, a large-scale military exercise encircling Taiwan with naval vessels, submarines, and aircraft. The exercise included live-fire drills and simulated blockade scenarios across all three maritime approaches to Taiwan. Multiple commercial vessels rerouted.

title: PLA Warship Confronts ROC Frigate — Median Line
description: People's Liberation Army Navy frigate crossed the Taiwan Strait median line and conducted a close-approach maneuver against a ROC Navy frigate on routine patrol. The PLA vessel came within 500 meters. ROC Navy issued radio challenges; PLA vessel did not respond before withdrawing west of the median line.
affectedRoutes: Taiwan Strait median line patrol zone

title: PLA Ballistic Missile Test — Taiwan Strait Zone
description: China's PLA Rocket Force conducted ballistic missile test firings into designated impact zones in the waters west of Taiwan. Japan's Joint Chiefs of Staff tracked the missiles and assessed two fell within Japan's Exclusive Economic Zone. Commercial air traffic diverted around test zones; shipping in the strait alerted.

title: PLA Coast Guard Blocks ROC Resupply — Dongsha
description: People's Republic of China coast guard vessels intercepted and blocked a ROC Coast Guard vessel attempting to deliver supplies to the ROC-administered Pratas Islands (Dongsha Atoll), forcing a 12-hour standoff. PRC vessels deployed water cannons before withdrawing following arrival of a second ROC vessel.

title: PLA PLAAF Intrusion — ADIZ Incursion
description: 52 PLA Air Force sorties entered Taiwan's Air Defense Identification Zone over a 24-hour period — the largest single-day ADIZ incursion in 2024. Aircraft included H-6 bombers, J-16 fighters, and Y-8 reconnaissance aircraft. ROC Air Force scrambled intercept flights and activated air defense systems.
affectedRoutes: Taiwan eastern air and sea approaches

title: Water Cannon Attack — Second Thomas Shoal
description: China Coast Guard vessels deployed water cannons against a Philippine Coast Guard vessel and a Bureau of Fisheries supply boat on a humanitarian resupply mission to the grounded BRP Sierra Madre at Second Thomas Shoal. Philippine sailors sustained minor injuries; resupply mission partially completed under duress.

title: Scarborough Shoal Blockade — Philippine Fishing Vessels
description: China Coast Guard and maritime militia vessels established a physical barrier using anchored boats and water hoses to prevent Philippine fishing vessels from accessing the Bajo de Masinloc (Scarborough Shoal) lagoon. Philippine Navy vessels dispatched to monitor. Standoff escalated diplomatic tensions between Manila and Beijing.

title: Vietnamese Fishing Vessel Rammed — Paracel Islands
source: Vietnam Ministry of Foreign Affairs / VOV
description: A Chinese coast guard vessel rammed and boarded a Vietnamese fishing boat near the PRC-administered Paracel Islands, confiscating the catch, fishing equipment, and navigation electronics. Crew of 17 released after several hours. Vietnam filed a formal diplomatic protest; China stated the vessel was operating illegally.

title: USNS Howard Confronted by PLA Frigate
description: US Navy surveillance vessel USNS Howard conducting a routine freedom-of-navigation operation in the South China Sea was confronted by a PLA Navy Type 054A frigate that issued demands to leave and conducted a close pass within 150 meters. US Navy assessed the PLA vessel's conduct as unprofessional and unsafe.

title: PLA Live-Fire Exercise — Spratly Islands
description: PLA Southern Theater Command conducted live-fire naval exercises in the vicinity of the disputed Spratly Islands, closing designated areas to commercial shipping for 72 hours. Exercises included destroyer and frigate fire drills and anti-submarine warfare exercises. Multiple commercial vessels rerouted around the exclusion zone.
affectedRoutes: South China Sea central shipping lane
